contact.demo_notice: The message really is stored. It lands in the demo database and can be read by anyone who signs in with the published credentials — so do not write anything you would not want others to see. It is deleted at the next nightly reset.

privacy.heading: Privacy in this demo
privacy.warning: Do not enter real personal data. The admin login is published openly on the front page. Anything you type into a form here — name, email, phone number, message text — can be read by anyone who signs in. Use invented details.
privacy.b1: Westengen Klinikk is an invented clinic. This site is a portfolio piece showing a complete booking and records system: customer-facing booking, calendar, client register, patient records, messages and an audit log. The practitioners, clients, bookings and notes in the demo are constructed, and refer to no real person.
privacy.b1b: This page is therefore not a privacy notice for a health service. It describes what the demo actually does with information you type in while trying it out.
privacy.b2: The demo is built and run by Westengen Studio (Markus Westengen). Questions about it can be sent through the contact form on the site. The contact details shown as the clinic’s — address, phone number and email — are placeholders and are not in use.
privacy.h3: What the demo stores about you
privacy.b3: Only what you type in yourself. Specifically:
privacy.b3_ul:
• Bookings: name, email, phone number, the time you chose and any notes you add.
  • Contact messages: name, email and the message text.
  • Waiting list and reviews: the fields the form asks for.
  • Technical: your IP address is used to limit how many forms can be sent per hour, and is not stored alongside the content.
privacy.b3b: The data sits with Supabase inside the EU. Nothing is shared onward, sold or used for marketing.
privacy.b4: Not long. The demo resets itself every day: everything visitors have entered is deleted and the setup returns to its starting point. You can also ask for something to be removed straight away through the contact form.
privacy.b5: The site sets no tracking or marketing cookies and uses no analytics tools. What is stored in your browser is:
privacy.b5_ul:
• Your language choice and your answer to the consent banner.
  • A temporary copy of a booking in progress, in case the connection drops.
  • A sign-in token from Supabase Auth — only if you log into the admin panel.
privacy.b5b: All of it lives in your own browser and disappears when you clear your browsing data.
privacy.b6: You can ask to see, correct or delete what you have entered. Send a message through the contact form and it will be done. If you believe data is being handled wrongly, you can complain to the Norwegian Data Protection Authority.
privacy.h7: What a real version would have
privacy.b7: In a real clinic installation this page is replaced by a full privacy notice with a legal basis under the GDPR, patient records under Norwegian health personnel law, retention periods, processor agreements and a subject-access routine. The system already has the machinery such a notice assumes: role-based access in the database, consent recorded at booking, and an audit log of every look at a patient record.
privacy.foot: Questions about privacy in the demo? Use the contact form on the site.
demo.heading: Sign in to the admin panel
demo.body1: Westengen Klinikk is an invented clinic. The interesting half sits behind the login: calendar, client register, patient records with consent and an audit log, service and practitioner administration, messages and waiting list.
demo.body2: Use one of the accounts below. Rows you create yourself are yours to edit and delete; the rows that came with the demo are write-protected, and everything resets every day.
demo.note_admin: Full access: every practitioner’s calendar, client register, patient records, services, practitioners and the audit log.
demo.note_therapist: Limited access: own calendar and own patients. Sign in with both to see the difference the role makes.
landing.heading: Booking and patient records for a small clinic
landing.body1: Customer-facing booking with live availability, cancellation by link, and a waiting list. Behind the login: a calendar per practitioner, a client register, patient records with consent and an audit log, service and practitioner administration, a message inbox and closed hours.
landing.body2: Westengen Klinikk does not exist. The clinic, the practitioners, the clients and every booking are invented. The setting is there only because a booking system needs somebody to book with.
landing.door_admin: Sign in to the admin panel
landing.door_public_p: How a customer meets the system. No sign-in, nothing to fill in first.
landing.door_public_1: Pick a therapist, service and time against real availability
landing.door_public_2: Cancel with a reference code, or join the waiting list
landing.door_public_3: Send a message and watch it land in the inbox behind
landing.door_admin_p: The interesting half needs a sign-in. Both accounts are right here.
landing.door_admin_1: Calendar, client register and patient records with consent
landing.door_admin_2: An audit log that catches every read, not just every change
landing.door_admin_3: Role-based access — sign in as both and see the difference
landing.creds_sub: Sign in with both to see what the role decides.
landing.inv1_p: Day, week and practitioner. Move, cancel or create appointments straight in the grid.
landing.inv2_p: Search, filtering, pagination and a colour bar per practitioner. Unassigned group bookings are set apart.
landing.inv3_p: Client cards with history. Records require registered consent, and every look-up is logged.
landing.inv4_p: Price, duration and visibility per service. Practitioners are deactivated, never deleted.
landing.inv5_p: An inbox fed by the contact form, and a FIFO queue that can be matched to free slots.
landing.inv6_p: Who did what, when. Visible to admin only, and editable by nobody.
landing.colophon1: You can create, edit and delete your own rows freely — the whole CRUD cycle is demonstrable. The rows that came with the demo are write-protected in the database: the buttons work, but the save is refused with an explanation, so the panel looks the same for the next visitor. Everything resets every day.
landing.colophon2: Do not enter real personal data. The login above is public, so anything you type can be read by anyone. More about what the demo stores.
landing.colophon3: A static frontend with no build step, Supabase underneath: PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security, Auth, Edge Functions and pg_cron. Six languages, and a PWA shell for staff.
contact.chain_heading: What happens when you press send
contact.chain_1: The browser checks the fields and length, and lets a hidden honeypot expose bots quietly.
contact.chain_2: An Edge Function receives it. Anon has no write access to the table, so the form cannot be abused straight against the database.
contact.chain_3: Turnstile and a rate limit are verified server-side, per IP address and per hour.
contact.chain_4: The message is stored with service_role and shows up in the admin inbox, marked new, read or answered.
contact.chain_foot: Sign in as admin@westengenklinikk.example to watch it arrive.
